title: Elizabeth Warren Says Americans' Instagram and Gmail Use Is Fueling the AI Boom— and They Deserve a 'Share in Its Success'
excerpt: On Monday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said Americans may be helping fuel the AI boom through everyday use of platforms such as Meta Platforms, Inc.’s In...
content_html:

On Monday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said Americans may be helping fuel the AI boom through everyday use of platforms such as Meta Platforms, Inc.'s Instagram and Gmail, owned by Alphabet Inc.'s Google, arguing that Big Tech should be taxed.

Elizabeth Warren Calls for AI Taxes

The Massachusetts Democrat raised the issue in a post on X, asking users whether they use Instagram or Gmail and warning that their online activity could be contributing to AI development.

Don't Miss:

  • A single bad hire can set a startup back years. Here are the 5 hires founders most often misjudge — and why

  • Still Learning the Market? These 50 Must-Know Terms Can Help You Catch Up Fast

"Big Tech has turned what all of us helped create into a trillion-dollar industry," Warren wrote. "It's time to tax AI so you can share in its success."

Do you use Instagram or Gmail?

You could be helping to train AI.

Big Tech has turned what all of us helped create into a trillion-dollar industry.

It's time to tax AI so you can share in its success.

— Elizabeth Warren (@SenWarren) August 3, 2026

Meta and Google did not immediately respond to Benzinga's request for comments.

Warren has previously called for policymakers to "tax AI and invest in people," arguing that rapid automation could widen economic inequality, displace workers and concentrate more wealth among major technology companies and wealthy investors.

She has also said the tax system should not encourage corporations to replace employees with machines.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Bernie Sanders Proposes $7 Trillion, AI Fund

In June, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) introduced legislation to give the public a financial stake in the growth of major AI companies.

Under the proposed American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, leading AI companies would make a one-time contribution equal to 50% of their stock to a federally managed investment fund. Sanders' office estimated that the fund could eventually grow to approximately $7 trillion.

AI Training Data Raises Privacy and Ownership Questions

The debate also highlights concerns over how user-generated content is collected and used to develop AI systems.

Poonacha Machaiah, co-founder of Cyberhuman.ai, wrote an article Medium, in which he said that the familiar phrase, "When something is free, you are the product," is especially relevant in the digital age.

伯尼·桑德斯提议设立 7 万亿美元的人工智能基金

六月，参议员。 伯尼·桑德斯 (佛蒙特州) 出台了立法，让公众在主要人工智能公司的发展中获得经济利益。

根据拟议的美国人工智能主权财富基金法案，领先的人工智能公司将一次性向联邦管理的投资基金捐款相当于其股票的 50%。 桑德斯办公室估计该基金最终可能增长至约 7 万亿美元。
